dct_description_sm: The decline of many migratory tundra caribou herds in Arctic Northern America worries many aboriginal communities that have used caribou for thousands of years. For example, the population of the Bathurst Caribou herd was 472,000-72,900 in 1986, and has since declined to 31,900-11,000 in 2008. Many factors (e.g. habitat, harvest, predators, diseases/parasites, extreme weather events and climate) may contribute to the decline. To understand how these factors interact and affect caribou abundance, we need to develop a comprehensive dataset of these factors in addition to measures of caribou productivity. The objective of this project is to define and develop habitat indicators on the winter range and along the pre-calving migration route of Bathurst Caribou. Specifically, we will (1) define habitat indicators for the winter range and pre-calving migration route; (2) develop historical datasets of these habitat indicators using field measurements, satellite remote sensing imagery, and climate records; and (3) analyse the relationships between climate variables and these habitat indicators.
dct_title_s: Migratory barren ground caribou habitat indicators using remote sensing, Nunavut
